findings.text: Any caller of launch takes the LP position of every earlier launch
Dust holders make harvest fail for every caller, forever
An attacker buys before harvest and takes most holder fees
The launcher can mint the pool position to their own address
pushDistribute pays by the balance at one instant
A launch with no mint takes the position id of the next launch
harvest does not check that the position is in the token pool
harvest fails with paired tokens that return no bool
Any caller can use a pending launch salt first
One blocked holder makes every harvest revert

The launcher runs router commands as the factory: Code smells: caller `preCommands` run with the factory as `msgSender`; Permit2 allowances with `type(uint48).max` expiry stay after use — A launcher can spend an old Permit2 allowance of the factory. We did not find a token balance that stays in the factory between transactions.

A fee-on-transfer paired token makes the payout larger than the balance: Code smells: `pushDistribute(userCut)` gets the requested amount, not the received amount — With a fee-on-transfer paired token, the last holder transfers revert. We did not confirm that a launcher would pick such a token.

The next launcher takes all ETH that the factory holds: Code smells: refund of `address(this).balance`, not the unused `msg.value`; open `receive()` — Any ETH that stays in the factory goes to the next caller of `launch`. We did not find a normal path that leaves ETH in the factory.

An attacker can initialize the pool first at a chosen price: Code smells: public salt, fixed pool key, `initializePool` does not revert on an existing pool, `amountOutMinimum` is 0 — An attacker can create the pool before the launch at a price the attacker chooses. We did not prove a profit from the seeded liquidity or the seed buys.

Contracts that hold the token receive fees that nobody claims: Code smells: only the factory and `POOL_MANAGER` are excluded from rewards — A v2 or v3 pair, a lending market or a bridge that holds the token gets a share of the fees that it cannot pass on. We did not measure the amount, or check if an attacker can skim it from a pair.

pushDistribute pays the nominal amount, not the amount received: Code smells: trusts the `amount` argument; unchecked `transfer` return values; any reward token the launcher chooses — A fee-on-transfer or rebasing reward token leaves the contract short, so the last transfers revert. We did not confirm which paired tokens the platform allows.

The rounding remainder of each payout stays in the token contract: Code smells: `amount * bal / total` rounds down; no sweep function for the reward token — The remainder of each payout stays in the token contract. The amount per harvest is small.
